items.title: Evaluate the finite radialized Gaussian test average

source.anchor: AppendixB2.2 Ex60: explicit radial integral on RHS of first equality, Gaussian evaluation in second equality; p4.4 and Eq21 genuine B6 specialization. Standing assumptions AppendixB2; B6 Eq15.
source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. ASTIS isolates the explicit analytic radial integral; the preceding identification with H(lambda) is not included.

items.statement: Let n>=3, kappa>=4 and lambda>=0, and draw O from the existing normalized Haar probability on the full real O(n). Put U=O_11, p=n/2 as a real number, a(O)=kappa+1+4lambda-(kappa-1)U, A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T), F(O)=det(O)sqrt(det A_O), N(O)=(sqrt(kappa)+1)U-(sqrt(kappa)-1), and J(O)=integral over real Euclidean n-space of exp(-a(O)||x||^2/4) against canonical volume. Every inner spatial integrand is absolutely integrable; F(O)J(O) and N(O)/a(O)^p are absolutely integrable under this Haar probability. Their finite expectations satisfy E[FJ]/(2pi)^p = [(-1)^(n-1)(sqrt(kappa)-1)^(n-1)/2^p] E[N/a^p]. This evaluates the explicit radialized iterated integral and does not identify it with the original mixture test H(lambda).
assumptions: Natural n>=3 and real kappa>=4 are the AppendixB2 standing range. Real lambda>=0 includes zero; no positive-lambda-only restriction is introduced.
The law is the actual canonical normalized full orthogonal Haar probability, with its inherited matrix topology and Borel sigma-algebra. A_O is the existing literal equation4 precision.

The inner domain is EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) with Euclidean norm and canonical volume. The exponent n/2 is real division, including half-integer dimensions; only the sign/normalizer powers n-1 use natural exponents.

All three absolute-integrability assertions are conclusions. No Gaussian density law, assumed Fubini equality, denominator bound, normalized-mixture identity or Borel/L1 weight is supplied by the caller.

obligations.label: Finite explicit radial Gaussian integral and actual B6 specialization

bindings.boundary: Only Ex60 Gaussian evaluation for its explicit radialized integral and the B6 specialization leading to the Eq21 right-hand side. Equality to original H(lambda), actual Gaussian probability laws and density normalization, conjugation/radialization of the original mixture, original Fubini/interchange, determinant-component half-mass, Haar-column sphere uniformity, Poisson identities, TV/radial/Hellinger separation, transcript/eigenbasis reductions and both main lower bounds remain separate obligations. The source-only sharp minor/path bounds inherited from B6 are not newly claimed; additional sharp domination constants in the source inventory are distinguishable from sufficient compact boundedness.

assumption_deltas.source: AppendixB2 n>=3,kappa>=4; lambda>=0; actual full Haar O(n), Euclidean dx, Eq4 precision. The denominator floor makes the B6 weight admissible.
assumption_deltas.lean: Same actual n/kappa/lambda range, canonical Haar/volume and literal precision. Inner/outer/final L1 assertions, denominator positivity and the actual B6 weight Borel/L1 facts are proved internally.
assumption_deltas.reason: The global continuous max extension agrees with the exact weight on every actual O_11. Finite compact bounds replace sharp domination only where sufficient, with no source repair, new binder or original H/Fubini claim.
